title: The displayed Euclidean recursion tests zero against zero.
details: Avigad, version 2007-01-09, §3.5.3 printed p. 77 (PDF81), displayed gcd recurrence. Visually checked: the first case tests0=0, so it always returns v and never reaches gcd(v mod u,u). This gives2 at(u,v)=(3,2) instead of1. Replace the condition by u=0. The recursive call then decreases the positive first argument because v mod u<u, and the usual Euclidean identity proves correctness. This is a local slip in an unused adjacent application; the recursion-theorem entry uses only §§3.4–3.5.1 and makes no gcd claim.
